content:
alina: Heads-up — noticed a P95 latency spike in prod after the host driver bump to 547.88. Autotuner started favoring the vectorized attention kernel for seq=512 and small batch sizes.

alina: numbers: baseline (driver 545) p95 ~ 130ms, after 547 bump p95 ~ 280ms on the same request mix. Token throughput down ~2.3x.

michael: Yikes. Which kernel path is being chosen now vs before?

alina: Before: attn->seqlen-path (sliced-kv + tiled-attn). After: attn->vec-accel (vectorized kernel with fused rotary). Autotuner weight for vec-accel jumped because of microbench on cuda 547 showing better peak perf for long GEMM shapes.

jin: Do we have perf counters or nvprof traces?

alina: Pushed a short profile to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/kernel-profiles/2067543210/vec_regressions.tar.gz. Key snippets: 

```
# sample from perf trace (512 seq, bs=1)
CUDA kernel: vec_accel_forward
avg SM occupancy: 22% (expected 48%)
L2 hit rate: 63% -> downhill compared to tiled path 81%
warp_stall: memory_dependency dominant
```

alina: Also kv-cache behavior changed: the vec path does worse for KV cache heavy hits because it spills more intermediate state leading to extra memcpy overhead. Observed extra ~1.1ms memcpy per layer.

samir: This smells like a driver scheduling heuristic change that exposed a throughput/latency tradeoff. Autotuner's benchmarking harness must have been run with synthetic long sequences and big batch sizes so vec path looked better. Our production is bs=1 with KV cache critical.

alina: Exactly. Autotuner scoring currently weights throughput more than KV-cache locality by default. That bias flipped the score on 547.

michael: Quick question: is this limited to H100 nodes or repro on A100 as well?

alina: Observed primarily on H100-p4d pools. A100 traces show smaller delta but still present on specific compute instances.

jin: Can we force the runtime to prefer tiled-attn for the affected model/route as a short-term mitigation?

alina: Yes — two options I tested:
1) Pin kernel via model config override: `kernel_preference: [tiled_attn, vec_accel]` — immediate in-memory change, no deploy.
2) Canary rollback of driver to 545 on a subset of hosts — heavier but matches baseline.

michael: Which is safer and lower risk for quick rollback?

alina: Pinning in config is lower risk and fast. I validated a canary: pinned model on 4 canary hosts -> p95 returned to ~135ms. No functional regressions.

samir: Awesome. We should still root-cause why autotuner selected vec_accel on 547. Is there a specific kernel timing metric that flipped?

alina: Yes: the autotuner measures end-to-end token/s on synthetic throughput tests. On 547 with long sequences the vec kernel had higher token/s; but it didn't account for KV memcpy microcosts (we don't simulate bs=1 online prefix cache in the harness). Also the driver changed warp scheduler heuristics so kernel start latency variance increased.

jin: So action items:
- short-term: config pin for affected models/routes (alina)
- mid-term: update autotuner harness to include KV-cache heavy workloads + bs=1 lat-focused scoring (samir)
- mid-term: add a weighted penalty for memcpy and start-latency variance to autotune score (michael)
- ops: prepare driver rollback playbook if config pin doesn't hold (jin/opsbot)

opsbot: I created a canary channel alert for hosts with driver 547.88 and abnormal p95 > 200ms. Link: https://console.redwood/alerts/547-canary

alina: Quick repro command for infra folks:
```
# run a short perf job that mimics production mix
python infra/bench/run_profile.py --model my-chat --seq 512 --bs 1 --kv_cache:true --reps 50 --driver 547.88
```

michael: Did you capture a flamegraph? that usually makes decode/memcpy hot paths obvious.

alina: Uploaded: gs://redwood-perf/flamegraphs/2067543210/vec-flame.svg. Top hot path shows `kernel->memcpy->cudaLaunch` chain repeated per layer.

samir: For audit I'd like the autotuner run id so we can replay: run id: autotune-run-2026-03-24-8741 (on perf cluster).

jin: I'll put a quick canary rollout plan in the runbook: pin config on 10% traffic for 1 hour, compare p95 and token-per-second, then escalate. If pinned hosts still have high p95, revert driver on the canary hosts.

michael: Also consider introducing a small hysteresis in autotuner decisions so we don't flip picks because of minor driver bumps. E.g., require >=3% stable win across 3 runs.

alina: Agreed. Also will add a KV-cache microbench to the harness (bs=1, prefix-heavy).

samir: Assignments: Alina will pin the config and post the exact config diff. Samir + Michael will draft autotune harness changes. Jin + Opsbot will prep rollback steps and a deploybot job to revert driver on canary hosts.

alina: Pushed the patch to override config: commit 9f3b2c1 (PR #4729) — PLEASE APPROVE if you can test quickly.

deploybot: deploy triggered for pinned-config -> canary subset (4 hosts). 2067543301: started

michael: I'll run the validation perf run against the canary now.

michael: Validation results: p95 dropped from 278ms -> 136ms on canary. Token/s recovered to within 5% of baseline.

jin: Good. Ops, if we don't see other regressions, do we proceed to ramp?

opsbot: Recommended ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 4h with automated health checks on p95, error rate, and token throughput.

samir: Postmortem follow-ups:
- update autotuner harness (owner: samir)
- add scheduling/driver compatibility tests to CI (owner: michael)
- document kernel selection hysteresis policy (owner: alina)

alina: I'll open the follow-up issues and tag infra/eng-runtime for traction. Thanks all for quick triage. :thumbsup:

michael: Thanks. Can we also log the regression in the perf-regressions tracker with links to traces and flamegraphs?

alina: Done: https://go.redwood/perf-regressions/2067543210

jin: Closing note — we should add an explicit KV-cache penalty to autotuner scoring before next scheduled autotune run.

alina: Agreed. I'll claim that and aim to get a PR up by EOD tomorrow.
